summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: North Carolina - N.C. Gen. Stat. § 7B-301 (Duty to report abuse, neglect, dependency)
North Carolina - Chapter 7B, Article 3 (Juvenile Code – abuse, neglect, dependency procedures)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 28 - JUVENILE JUSTICE AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION (TRANSFERRED TO TITLE 14B)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of North Carolina
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals vacated the visitation portion of a dispositional order because the trial court improperly delegated visitation entirely to the discretion of the custodian instead of establishing an appropriate court-approved visitation plan.
key_cases.relevance: Court-set visitation is the practical engine of reunification and may not be delegated away.
key_cases.quote: The trial court maintains the responsibility to ensure that an appropriate visitation plan is established within the dispositional order.

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that evidence of neglect predating loss of custody, including a prior adjudication, is admissible in a termination proceeding, but the trial court must make an independent present-day determination that weighs changed conditions against the history of neglect and the probability that neglect would recur.
key_cases.relevance: Ballard is the authority a parent invokes to show corrected conditions supporting reunification rather than termination.
key_cases.quote: The trial court must also consider any evidence of changed conditions in light of the evidence of prior neglect and the probability of a repetition of neglect.

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that a parent's failure to comply with a court-approved case plan supports termination under N.C.G.S. § 7B-1111(a)(2) so long as the case plan provision addresses an issue that directly or indirectly contributed to the child's removal, and it reversed the Court of Appeals' contrary, narrower reading.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable progress on nexus-related case plan components is what supports a return home rather than termination.
key_cases.quote: parental compliance with a judicially adopted case plan is relevant in determining whether grounds for termination exist

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and held that the trial court had authority under N.C.G.S. § 7B-904(d1)(3) to require the mother to create a budgeting plan, and that her failure to do so supported termination under § 7B-1111(a)(2) because her mismanagement of income worsened the instability and inadequate housing that led to the juveniles' removal.
key_cases.relevance: It defines what counts as reasonable progress in correcting the conditions that led to removal, the measure by which a return home is assessed.
key_cases.quote: it was entirely appropriate for the court to have ordered respondent to create a budgeting plan

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and held that a permanency planning order ceasing reunification need not recite N.C.G.S. § 7B-507's language verbatim so long as its findings address the substance of the statutory requirements, and that an incomplete cease-reunification order may be cured by the findings in the later termination of parental rights order reviewed together with it.
key_cases.relevance: It governs the point at which reunification ceases to be the plan, and therefore the findings a parent must attack to preserve a return home.
key_cases.quote: When reviewing the sufficiency of such orders, an appellate court should consider whether the trial court's findings of fact address the substance of the statutory requirements.

state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county department of social services where the child lives — the county list is at ncdhhs.gov/divisions/social-services/local-dss-directory

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (voluntary agreement; must meet education, employment, or disability conditions; N.C. Gen. Stat. § 108A-48(c))

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
